findings.title: getCredentials NPE for unknown/local users
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` then dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without a null check. getMyUser returns null when the username is not in the `users` map (e.g. a purely local DB user). Other methods like isConfiguredFor and isValid guard against null. The new override will therefore throw NullPointerException for any user not known to this storage when the credential-manager enumerates federated credentials, breaking login / credential listing for local users.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
findings.body: On successful recovery-code use the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()`. That API only removes a locally stored (DB) credential. When the credential was created in user storage via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, there is no local credential to remove; the federated credential must be disabled/removed via disableCredentialType / federated path. As written, an exhausted federated recovery-code set is left in the external storage, so the user keeps an empty/used credential and the cleanup semantic diverges between local and federated users.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean does `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` then unconditionally `credentialModelOpt.get()`. If no federated nor local recovery credential exists (race, deleted credential, mis-configured flow) this throws NoSuchElementException during login form rendering, producing a 500 instead of a handled error. The previous code had the same pattern but the new helper explicitly returns Optional to signal absence and callers should handle the empty case.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes handed to user storage in clear text
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes to JSON and passes them as UserCredentialModel to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential()`. The local path stores `credentialModel` which contains only hashed codes via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, but the federated path persists the raw codes. Any UserStorageProvider that simply stores `input.getChallengeResponse()`/`getValue()` (as the bundled test provider does) will keep all 12 recovery codes in clear text outside Keycloak DB with no hashing or single-use consumption enforced by the helper, weakening the security property that recovery codes are stored hashed.
